pharm: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication; long half-life allows once-daily dosing.
quick: 400 mg orally once daily (UTI/bronchitis); duration per indication
May be taken with or without food; separate from cation antacids/iron/zinc
Avoid; fluoroquinolones generally not recommended in pregnancy
Avoid; fluoroquinolones generally not recommended while breastfeeding
Reduce dose in significant renal impairment (renally eliminated)
No major adjustment; renal clearance predominates
Avoid excess; may worsen CNS effects
Tendon pain, CNS effects, photosensitivity, QT, glucose
summary: Lomefloxacin is a long-acting fluoroquinolone antibacterial historically used for uncomplicated and complicated urinary tract infections and acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, and as surgical/transurethral prophylaxis. It inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. It is notable for pronounced phototoxicity and shares the fluoroquinolone class risks of tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, QT prolongation, and aortic aneurysm. It is no longer marketed in the United States; this record is compiled from class labeling and pharmacopeial/EMA-type references.
indications: Uncomplicated and complicated urinary tract infections caused by susceptible organisms
Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis caused by susceptible organisms
Preoperative prophylaxis for transurethral surgical procedures (per historical labeling)

dosage.d: 400 mg once daily for 3-10 days depending on organism
Reduce dose (e.g., 400 mg loading then 200 mg once daily) for CrCl 10-40 mL/min

admin: Take with plenty of fluids; may be taken with or without food
Separate by at least 2-4 hours from antacids, sucralfate, iron, zinc, or multivitamins containing cations
Avoid sun and UV exposure during and for several days after treatment (strong phototoxicity)
Stop at first sign of tendon pain or neuropathy
moa: Lomefloxacin inhibits the bacterial type II topoisomerases DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, enzymes required for DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination. Inhibition causes bacterial DNA strand breakage and cell death, giving concentration-dependent bactericidal activity against many Gram-negative and some Gram-positive organisms.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to lomefloxacin or other quinolones
relative: History of tendon disorders associated with quinolones
Known QT prolongation or with QT-prolonging drugs
Children, adolescents, pregnancy, and lactation (cartilage concerns)
monitor: Phototoxic skin reactions and QT interval

preg: Fluoroquinolones, including lomefloxacin, are generally avoided in pregnancy because of concerns about effects on developing cartilage; use only if no safer alternative exists and benefit clearly outweighs risk.
lact: Fluoroquinolones may be excreted in breast milk and are generally avoided during breastfeeding because of potential effects on the infant's joints; use an alternative where possible.
renal: Lomefloxacin is eliminated largely unchanged by the kidneys and accumulates in renal impairment; reduce the dose (typically a normal loading dose then halved maintenance) based on creatinine clearance.
hepatic: Hepatic metabolism is minor; no major dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment, but monitor as for the class.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, etc.) - additive QT prolongation/torsades risk
Corticosteroids - increased risk of tendon rupture, especially in older patients
moderate: Multivalent cations (antacids, sucralfate, iron, zinc, calcium, magnesium) - markedly reduce absorption; separate dosing
NSAIDs - may increase CNS stimulation and seizure risk
minor: Caffeine/theophylline - quinolones may raise levels (lomefloxacin effect modest)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; dairy and cation-containing products reduce absorption if taken together.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol, which may compound CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause dysglycemia; monitor blood glucose in diabetics.

counsel: Avoid sunlight and tanning beds during treatment and for a few days after - this drug causes strong sun sensitivity
Stop the medicine and call your doctor if you get tendon, joint, or muscle pain, or tingling/numbness
Do not take antacids, iron, or calcium/zinc supplements within a few hours of your dose
Report severe or bloody diarrhea, palpitations, or unusual mood changes
pk: Plasma peak ~1-2 hours after an oral dose
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Not currently FDA-approved/marketed in the US (withdrawn); this record is compiled from fluoroquinolone class labeling and EMA/pharmacopeial references rather than an active openFDA label
Among the most phototoxic fluoroquinolones - strict sun avoidance is essential
Carries the full fluoroquinolone class warnings: tendinopathy, neuropathy, CNS effects, QT prolongation, aortic aneurysm
Predominantly renally cleared - reduce dose in renal impairment
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Manage by gastric emptying if early and supportive care; ensure adequate hydration. Monitor ECG for QT prolongation and watch for CNS excitation/seizures. Lomefloxacin is not significantly removed by dialysis.
